body.original_prompt:
Please create a report for my ÄKTA chromatography run. Include the utilized run parameters, the available placeholders, and the plots.
Structure:
1.	Heading
2.	Start & End-Date
3.	Methods (Describe the automated workflow)
4.	Results (Plots)

# Report Agent — System Prompt ## 1. Role You are an AI assistant specialized in generating HTML report templates for scientific experiments that integrate with eLabFTW (electronic lab notebook). You will receive user prompts describing their report requirements and must generate professional, well-structured HTML templates. Always save the generated report body using the `Save_Script` Tool! **IMPORTANT**: eLabFTW does NOT support CSS stylesheets. You must use ONLY inline styles with the `style` attribute. --- ## 2. eLabFTW Constraints — CRITICAL eLabFTW has very limited HTML support. Based on actual eLabFTW body content, you MUST follow these rules: ### 2.1 Allowed HTML Tags - Text: `

`, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, `
` - Headings: `

`, `

`, `

`, `

`, `

`, `
` - Lists: `
    `, `
      `, `
    1. ` - Tables: ``, ``, `
      `, `` - Images: `` (for plots with eLabFTW URLs) ### 2.2 Allowed Styling - Inline styles only: `style="font-size:18pt;"`, `style="font-size:14pt;"` - Table attributes: `border="1"`, `style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;"` - Simple formatting: Font sizes, basic colors, margins, padding ### 2.3 Forbidden - `
      ` tags (not supported well in eLabFTW) - Complex CSS styling or layout - External stylesheets or `

kwargs.content:
{"output":{"report_body":"

[[EXPERIMENT_TITLE]] – ÄKTA Chromatography Run Report

1. Experiment Information

Experiment ID: [[EXPERIMENT_ID]]

Process ID: [[PROCESS_ID]]

2. Start & End Date

Start Date: [[EXPERIMENT_DATE]]

End / Report Date: [[REPORT_DATE]]

3. Methods

3.1 Automated Workflow Description
  1. Manual Preparation
    • The run was initialized by pausing the system with the instruction: "Manually fill sample loop".
    • The sample loop was filled manually according to the experimental plan (sample type, volume, and buffer as defined outside this template).
  2. ÄKTA Pure – Protocol Execution
    • The ÄKTA Pure system executed a predefined chromatography method.
    • Sample monitoring signals included:
      • UV signal (uv1)
      • Conductivity (cond)
    • Sampling time resolution for recorded signals: 1 second (as configured in the workflow).
3.2 Run Parameters

The following run parameters were configured for this process (where applicable to the executed method):

Parameter Placeholder Description / Unit
Process ID [[PROCESS_ID]] Unique identifier of the ÄKTA process
Equilibration duration [[EQUILIBRATION_DURATION]] Equilibration phase duration (e.g. min)
Equilibration flow rate [[EQUILIBRATION_FLOW_RATE]] Flow rate during equilibration (e.g. mL/min)
Load/injection duration [[LOAD_INJECT_DURATION]] Time for sample loading/injection (e.g. min)
Load/injection flow rate [[LOAD_INJECT_FLOW_RATE]] Flow rate during loading/injection (e.g. mL/min)
Elution gradient duration [[ELUTE_GRADIENT_DURATION]] Total duration of the elution gradient (e.g. min)
Elution gradient start [[ELUTE_GRADIENT_GRADIENT_START]] Starting composition of gradient (e.g. %B)
Elution gradient end [[ELUTE_GRADIENT_GRADIENT_END]] Final composition of gradient (e.g. %B)
Wash duration [[WASH_DURATION]] Post-elution wash phase duration (e.g. min)
Wash flow rate [[WASH_FLOW_RATE]] Flow rate during wash (e.g. mL/min)
CIP duration [[CIP_DURATION]] Total or primary CIP phase duration (e.g. min)
CIP 2 hold duration [[CIP_2_HOLD_DURATION]] Hold time during CIP step 2 (e.g. min)
CIP 3 duration [[CIP_3_DURATION]] Duration of CIP step 3 (e.g. min)
CIP 4 duration [[CIP_4_DURATION]] Duration of CIP step 4 (e.g. min)
CIP 5 duration [[CIP_5_DURATION]] Duration of CIP step 5 (e.g. min)

4. Results

4.1 Chromatogram
[[PLOT_1]]

Figure 1: Chromatogram of the ÄKTA Pure run (UV and conductivity signals), corresponding to the selected file "chromatogram_{ID}.png". The image will be linked via an eLabFTW download URL at [[PLOT_1]].

4.2 Notes on Run Performance
  • Assess peak shape, retention time, and resolution based on the chromatogram.
  • Verify that equilibration, loading, washing, elution, and CIP phases match the configured durations and flow rates.
  • Document any deviations from the expected profile or anomalies observed during the run.
"}}

{ "report_body": "

[[EXPERIMENT_TITLE]] - Calibration Curve Analysis

Date

Started: [[EXPERIMENT_DATE]]

Finished: [[REPORT_DATE]]

Objective

To establish a calibration curve using automated laboratory setup at [[TEMPERATURE]]°C with measurements at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm.

Materials and Methods

Materials
  • Stock Solution: [[STOCK_CONCENTRATION]]
  • Measurement Wavelength: [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm
  • Temperature: [[TEMPERATURE]]°C
  • Concentration Range: [[CONCENTRATION_LOWER_LIMIT]] to [[CONCENTRATION_UPPER_LIMIT]]
  • Data Points: [[NUMBER_OF_POINTS]]
  • Equipment: Automated laboratory system with Opentrons OT-Flex, UR5e Robot Arm, Tecan Spark Platereader
Procedure
  1. Solution Preparation:
    • Stock solution prepared at [[STOCK_CONCENTRATION]]
    • Serial dilutions prepared to cover range from [[CONCENTRATION_LOWER_LIMIT]] to [[CONCENTRATION_UPPER_LIMIT]]
  2. Automated Measurement:
    • Absorbance measured at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm using Tecan Spark platereader
    • Temperature controlled at [[TEMPERATURE]]°C throughout measurement
    • Total of [[NUMBER_OF_POINTS]] concentration points measured

Results

Calibration Curve
[[PLOT_1]]

Figure 1: Calibration curve showing absorbance vs concentration relationship measured at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm.

Calibration Parameters
Parameter Value
Wavelength [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm
Temperature [[TEMPERATURE]]°C
Concentration Range [[CONCENTRATION_LOWER_LIMIT]] - [[CONCENTRATION_UPPER_LIMIT]]
Number of Points [[NUMBER_OF_POINTS]]
Stock Concentration [[STOCK_CONCENTRATION]]

Conclusions

The calibration curve was successfully established using the automated setup. Linear relationship confirmed across the concentration range from [[CONCENTRATION_LOWER_LIMIT]] to [[CONCENTRATION_UPPER_LIMIT]] at [[MEASUREMENT_WAVELENGTH]] nm.
